rule: A contract changes only by a new version. The spec, every implementer and the tests change in the same commit, and the change is recorded in decisions.jsonl. tests/run_tests.py checks that every file below carries the current marker.

contracts.what: What the decision and challenge ledgers say is open, settled, in force or contested, decided once (tools/lifecycle.py) and shared by check_ledgers, status, export, the MCP server and the cockpit. A supersedes takes effect only from a settled line (adopted closes any earlier decision; rejected and superseded settle a proposal only and cannot retire an adopted decision); a proposed line is a proposed replacement; a resolves only from a resolved or accepted-risk line; self, forward and unknown references are problems and take no effect; more than one effective closer is a conflict, kept, not collapsed. Applicability of an adopted decision: standing ('adopted, no structured supersession found'), superseded, revoked (revokes), expired or not yet effective (effective_from/until); amends (an id or {id, clauses}) records a partial amendment. Export records gain applicability, closed_by, proposed_replacements, amended_by, conflict, transition_problems (decisions) and open, closed_by, conflict (challenges); in_force follows these rules. Adopting a proposal replaces what it proposed to replace; a closing and a revoking line on one record is a conflict; an amendment lapses with what it amends; effective dates are evaluated against the ledger's latest date by every reader; check_ledgers reports invalid transitions on earlier lines as warnings. export and mcp stay @1 with this deviation recorded in docs/lifecycle.md.
tests: lifecycle: the six review reproductions and the other fixture cases resolve as specified
lifecycle: check_ledgers refuses exactly the cases with a transition that takes no effect
lifecycle: status, export, the MCP server and the cockpit show the same open items and in-force decisions
lifecycle: a transition that takes no effect on an earlier line is a warning, so later appends still work; a new one is refused

contracts.what: Read-only static control surface over a records store: DIR/index.html (one self-contained page: Choices, Topology, Budget, Run/Drift and the other v0.4 surfaces) and DIR/cockpit.json (the data it was built from). Choices compose paste-ready ledger_append / handoff set lines and write nothing (DEC-019). Reads decisions, challenges, handoff@1/@2, threads.md and conversation@1 through the export@1 readers, plus governance/budget.jsonl; changes none of them. Deterministic; no clock is read (the newest record, the records revision and its commit and fetch times are shown, not today). @2 (HO-RK-20261105-VZH4): each choice says what it asks (the proposer's optional `ask`, else a summary labelled derived), what cites it and waits on it, its age, and whether it may be overtaken (later citations; opt-in build-time PR states); Amend and Clarify compose ledger lines (an amending adopted line; an open question challenge addressed to the proposer); Inquire copies an off-record prompt; Questions lists open questions. @3 (HO-RK-20261105-SWK5): a Pull requests surface rendering governance/pr-state.jsonl (relay-kit/prs@1): each PR's What / Why / How / Authorized verbatim with who wrote it (an agent's Author: line is tagged as not the owner's), missing sections, reviews with their family and whether one is from another family than the author, CI, and read times; PR states for the overtaken check come from that file, so --pr-state only fills gaps. --theme FILE (known colour variables and font lists only; an optional light scheme with a toggle) and --landing SURFACE. The page still fetches and writes nothing. Additive: nothing in @2 changed meaning. @4 (HO-RK-20261105-8DTW): reads the ledgers through relay-kit/lifecycle@1 (a proposal leaves Choices only when a settled line closes it; a proposed replacement is shown on its card; transitions that take no effect or conflict are listed on Review); every composed decision or challenge line carries --expect ID=STATE@HASH (and one for what a proposal replaces) so ledger_append refuses it, with what changed, once the item has moved on; the header shows the records' revision, commit time and last fetch (aged in the browser) apart from the newest record. Nothing from @3 was removed. @5 (HO-RK-20261106-NXPR; DEC-139, DEC-140): Pull requests folds each review under its card with author, family (signed, or inferred from the login via review_families or the records' .ledger.json 'actors' map, and labelled so; else unsigned), kind (review or review-style comment), verdict, time, inline-comment count, and the body verbatim as escaped paragraphs and lists (no markdown executed, URLs as text); a 'Findings: N blocking / M should-fix' line only when the body states those counts. A Status surface (11, a --landing target) renders the newest relay-kit/status@1 edition verbatim from a markdown subset, tags its author, flags it stale past --drift-days (measured from the newest record), and indexes older editions. Choices show relay-kit/decision-support@1 notes per item, one block per author in reading order (independent authors, the owner, then the coordinator lane), latest per author with history, and 'no decision-support note yet' otherwise; the ledger mechanics (what each action does) sit behind a 'how the ledger records this' disclosure. Decision, challenge and decision-support text is rendered with its structure: (1)…(n) enumerations, numbered or dashed lines and line breaks become lists and paragraphs, escaped, never markdown. cockpit.json gains status, decision_support, choices[].support, reviews' kind/body/family_source/findings/comments, and counts.status_editions/support_notes/choices_without_support. Nothing from @4 was removed. @6 (HO-CKPT-20261106-D1C5, HO-CKPT-20261107-EBVA; DEC-141 run 1 items 7–11, DEC-151): the information topology draws each handoff from the sender's rim (a dot) to the receiver's rim (a large arrowhead) with its count in a pill beside the arrowhead, never mid-span; opposite directions bend to opposite sides; a self-handoff is a visible loop above the node with its count; actors step across columns band by band; a lane with no line in threads.md is tagged 'no thread' on its band; a per-actor table (sent, received, to itself, busiest counterpart each way) carries the same counts as the edges; cockpit.json's topology.information gains actors[] and lanes_without_thread, lane nodes has_thread. An Actions surface (12, a --landing target) renders the human action list (relay-kit/actions@1: --actions FILE, else every actions/*.md in the records store) as written: open items with since-when and age to the newest record, size and due date when the author stated them (else 'not stated'), done items folded, 'needs you' styling; the page ticks nothing and infers nothing. cockpit.json gains actions and counts.actions_open/actions_done. Nothing from @5 was removed. @7 (HO-AEC-20261111-2CY6): a Coordination surface (13, a --landing target; tools/coordination.py) reads chat-telemetry's own output saved under telemetry/chat/*.json (re-measuring nothing) and draws a turn timeline, the owner's reply gaps (gaps ending in an owner-typed turn; bands and the median under 15 minutes; wall clock, not effort), turns by local hour, message length per turn, a per-thread table, hangs and longest silences, and governed vs autonomous with stretches; owner turns are a lower bound shown beside the ledgers' owner decision and challenge lines in the same days; raw captures no output covers are listed; with no output the half is unknown with a reason, never zero; previews of the owner's words are dropped. Its ledger half gathers telemetry@2's coordination_loss, idea_to_completed_handoff_latency and measurement_coverage, and marks handoff stage times not derived. cockpit.json gains coordination. Nothing from @6 was removed.

contracts.what: governance/pr-state.jsonl, append-only, written by relay-kit prs at build time from GitHub (gh CLI or a token): a 'pr' line when a pull request's state changed since its last line (repo, number, url, title, state open|closed|merged, draft, author, author_line from the body's Author: line, times, base, head, reviews [{by, verdict, at, signed, stated}], ci {state success|failure|pending|none, failing}, body_sections {what, why, how, authorized} verbatim with HTML comments removed, missing, truncated) and a 'fetch' line per run (ts, via, repos, ok, failed, since_days, prs_seen, appended). Repositories from handoffs/.ledger.json 'repos' or --repo. The one GitHub reader for pull requests: the Cockpit and other readers read the file. @2 (HO-RK-20261105-TXRM step 1): pull requests are read through tools/github.py, the kit's read-only client for pull-request reads (GET only; pagination; retries with backoff; rate-limit waits or refusal with the reset time; one fetch per path per run; optional ETag cache). A pr line gains `unread` (reviews or ci that couldn't be read: missing is not zero; ci state 'unknown'); the fetch line gains `coverage` per repository (what was asked, listed, more_available, re-read open PRs, PRs read, partial reads), `revisions` (default branch and pushed_at) and `client` (requests, retries, waits, cache hits, rate limit left, first/last request time). @1 lines stay readable. @3 (HO-RK-20261106-NXPR, DEC-139): each review carries id, kind 'review', its body verbatim (cut at 4000 characters, truncated: true) and comments (its inline-comment count; the inline text stays on GitHub); issue comments that are reviews in all but type (first non-empty line opening with Review / Execution review / Reviewer, or a verdict stated in the opening words) are recorded as reviews with kind 'comment', verdict null and the same fields; unread may say 'comments'. One more read per PR (issue comments) and one per PR with reviews (inline comments). @1 and @2 lines stay readable; a PR whose reviews gained bodies gets one new line on the first @3 run, an unchanged PR none.
tests: prs: body sections are kept verbatim; missing and comment-only sections are listed as missing
prs: an unchanged PR appends no new line; a changed one appends one, and every run appends a fetch line
prs: a failing repository is recorded in the fetch line and the others are still read
prs: it writes only governance/pr-state.jsonl and never rewrites a line
prs: CI state from check runs and statuses; reviews keep the verdict stated in their body
prs: repositories come from .ledger.json repos or --repo; anything not OWNER/NAME is refused
prs: a PR last recorded open is read again however old, so a closed one never stays open
prs: appending to a file without a final newline doesn't join two lines
github: pages walks pages until the limit or a short page, and says whether more were available
github: network errors and 5xx are retried with backoff; other errors and exhausted retries are refused with the status
github: a rate limit waits for the reset when it is short, and is refused with the reset time when it isn't
github: a path is fetched once per run; with a cache folder an unchanged resource is revalidated by its ETag
github: the gh transport only ever sends GET, and parses status and headers from its output
prs: what was asked for and what came back is recorded per repository; unreadable reviews or CI are unread, not none
prs: a PR that can't be read again is a partial read, not a failed repository; an unread part keeps its last value, recorded once as unread
prs: review bodies are recorded verbatim (cut at 4000, flagged), with inline-comment counts; review-style issue comments join as kind comment
prs: review-style comments that can't be read are unread, keep their last value, and never read as none
prs: success, then a failed read with unchanged content, then a successful retry: each transition is one pr line, and the retry clears unread (Kate 1 on #33)
prs: review submissions are walked past the first 100; past the per-PR cap, coverage is reported as partial (Kate 7 on #33)

contracts.what: A hand-written status edition: status/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<edition>.md in the records store, with front matter date, edition, author, covers (and contract) and the four H2 sections Accomplishments / Road bumps / Status / Next steps, in a markdown subset (ATX headings, lists, bold, italic, inline code, horizontal rules, fenced code shown as text; links shown as text; HTML comments removed; anything else plain text). Editions are added, never edited or rewritten; the newest is the latest date, then morning < midday < noon < afternoon < evening < night, then other names alphabetically. The Cockpit renders it as written; `relay-kit edition new` scaffolds one and `check` reports what doesn't fit. Adopted from the pilot form kairos/status@0, which has the same fields.
tests: status: `relay-kit edition new` scaffolds the front matter and four headings and never overwrites; `check` reports what doesn't fit
cockpit: Status renders the newest edition verbatim from the markdown subset (escaped; links as text), indexes older ones, and can be the landing
status: `edition new` refuses a --covers value that could add a key or end the front matter: newline, duplicate key, terminator (Kate 2 on #33)
status: a dangling status-file symlink is refused by `edition new` (its target outside the records is never created) and reported by the reader (Kate 3 on #33)
status: a file named for a date that doesn't exist (2026-13-03) is unreadable, and the Cockpit still builds (Kate 4 on #33)
status and decision support: a missing or empty contract marker fails `edition check` and makes a support line unreadable (Kate 5 on #33)

contracts.what: governance/decision-support.jsonl, append-only: one line per authored decision-support note, {id, item (the DEC/CH/HO id it is about), author (actor with session), at, contract, changes_if_accepted, unchanged, counterfactual, can_wait, depends, recommendation}, all free text written by the author named; the latest line per (item, author) is current and earlier ones are its history. Nothing in it is generated. Readers show one block per author in a reading order (independent authors, the owner, then the coordinator lane) and rank nothing. Lines of the pilot form kairos/decision-support@0 (same fields) are read as @1.
tests: cockpit: decision-support notes render per item, one block per author, independent authors before the coordinator, latest per author with history; mechanics folded
status and decision support: a missing or empty contract marker fails `edition check` and makes a support line unreadable (Kate 5 on #33)

contracts.what: governance/budget.jsonl, append-only: @1's ts, actor, window, tokens_in, tokens_out (and optional agents, note) plus @2's id (or a content-hash id for older lines), method (measured | proxy | estimate; required on new lines, 'unlabelled' for older ones), interval_start/end, includes_children {included, ids}, correction_of (an earlier line, same window: the replaced line is never summed with its correction and its use keeps the replaced line's time; two corrections of one line are a reported conflict, the later counting), metric_version, scope and source. Read through tools/budget.py by every reader; written by relay-kit budget-append. tokens_detail {input, output, cache_write, cache_read, by_model} keeps cache reads apart. relay-kit usage-ingest (tools/usage_ingest.py) turns a Claude Code session's local logs into one line per session: measured when the logs are complete, an estimate marked complete:false (a lower bound, with log_coverage) when compacted or late (message ids counted once across main and subagent logs; costUSD unused; re-ingesting appends a correction; no paths in the line).
tests: budget: a correction replaces the line it names; the two are never summed
budget: a parent that includes its children's use isn't counted with them
budget: new lines must say how they were measured; malformed @2 fields are refused
budget: two corrections of one line are a conflict, reported; only the later one counts
budget: older lines without a method count as 'unlabelled', never as measured
budget: a correction is counted at the time of the line it replaces, so relabelling never moves use into this week
budget: children are followed through corrections, inclusion is inherited, and self, later, cross-window and cyclic references are reported and ignored
budget: the same reading appended twice gets two ids; duplicate ids in the file are reported and both lines read; a corrected line can't be corrected again
usage: one measured line per session; a message split over several log lines counts once; cache reads stay apart
usage: ingesting a session again appends a correction, so the cockpit counts it once
usage: the line carries counts and the session id only: no file paths or folder names
usage: a compacted log, or one starting well after its session did, gives an estimate marked incomplete, never a measurement
usage: a re-run that shows less than before is refused; duplicate session lines are refused; unidentified usage lines and zone-less times aren't counted

contracts.what: A derived view (tools/telemetry.py, relay-kit telemetry), rebuilt from the records and never stored in them: compute_consumption, delivery_throughput, lead_time, review_burden, post_merge_remediation (14 and 30 days, mature cohorts only), surviving_changes, human_intervention, idea_to_completed_handoff_latency (DEC-162's progress proxy: a recorded 'Idea captured: <time>' in a handoff's Task or Context section to its first completed step; measured only when both exist; invalid, future or reversed markers excluded by name), measurement_coverage and coordination_loss, each with a frozen definition, a version, a measured/proxy/estimate/derived/unknown label, --lane and --content metadata as the cockpit applies them, distributions (median, p90, n) and 'unknown' with a reason in place of zero. No composite score, no targets. The cockpit's Review surface shows it.
tests: telemetry: every metric carries its definition, version and label; with no records each says unknown, never zero
telemetry: lead time and review burden are distributions from pr-state; abandoned PRs are counted apart
telemetry: remediation is counted only over cohorts old enough; only a fix or revert wording right before this repository's reference counts
telemetry: corrections and child runs are applied before compute is summed; a malformed line is counted invalid, as the cockpit counts it, and breaks nothing
telemetry: the cockpit's Review panel shows each metric with its label and definition, no score or target, at the page's as of
telemetry: the view is derived and is never written into the records
telemetry: --content metadata reads no free text (claims and remediation are unknown); --lane keeps other lanes' handoffs and sessions out
telemetry: a time after the last pull-request read doesn't move as_of; it is flagged instead

telemetry: capture latency is measured only from a marker in a handoff's Task or Context and a completed step; markers elsewhere, invalid, future or reversed are excluded by name, other lanes left out, metadata unknown, never zero

contracts.what: A hand-kept human action list: a markdown file (one given as --actions FILE to the Cockpit, or any actions/*.md in the records store) in which `- [ ]` lines are open items and `- [x]` lines (or struck-through text) are done; the heading above a line is its section; `Since YYYY-MM-DD`, `Due YYYY-MM-DD` and a size such as `~15 min`, `2 min`, `1 h`, `one word each` are read out of the line only when the author wrote them, else null. Items are appended and ticked, never deleted. Readers render the lines as written (inline markdown subset) and tick, rank or generate nothing. Pilot form: kairos/actions-zach.md (DEC-151).
tests: cockpit: Actions renders a markdown checklist as written: open items with since/age, size and due when stated, done items folded; --actions FILE or actions/*.md; a landing target

contracts.what: Read-only MCP server over a records store, JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, protocol revisions 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 (any other gets -32022 with the supported list): the tool names and arguments, relaykit:// resource URIs, the result envelope (schema, evidence_class as in export@1, provenance 'read from <path> at records sha256:<hash>', content_level, notice) and the --content metadata policy. No tool writes to the records (DEC-019).
tests: mcp: initialize handshake, tools/list and ping over stdio, for each supported protocol version
mcp: a 2026-07-28 or unknown protocol version gets -32022 with the supported list, never a silent fallback
mcp: every read tool answers with evidence_class and a provenance line naming the records hash
mcp: with --content metadata no tool or resource returns record text, and text filters are refused

mcp: malformed JSON-RPC gets a proper error and the server keeps serving
